title: Linear regression and Pearson r
intro: Fit y on x, then read direction and make a prediction.

beats.spoken: Start with two named lists. Values on the same row belong to the same observation.
beats.coach: Lists xval and yval are already named. Each row is one observation: for example, x = 1 is paired with y = 2.

beats.spoken: In Lists and Spreadsheet, open Statistics, then Stat Calculations. Choose the m x plus b form.
beats.coach: Menu → 4 Statistics → 1 Stat Calculations → 3 Linear Regression (mx+b).

beats.spoken: Use the right arrow to choose the list named x val for X, then Tab. Choose the list named y val for Y.
beats.coach: From X List: Right to open; Tab confirms xval and moves to Y. Right to open Y, Right again to select yval, then Tab.

beats.spoken: Use each pair once. Keep the fitted equation in f one and the results starting in C.
beats.coach: Check Frequency List 1, store to f1 and results in C. Press Enter to calculate.

beats.spoken: Read m and b. The slope is the change in predicted y per extra unit of x.
beats.coach: m = 1.4 and b = 0.5, so ŷ = 1.4x + 0.5. Each extra unit of x adds 1.4 to the prediction.

beats.spoken: Read the two rows separately. r is positive here and gives the upward direction.
beats.coach: Pearson r ≈ 0.990 gives the positive direction; r² = 0.98 is a separate output.

beats.spoken: A falling pattern can have the same r squared. Use the unsquared r to tell which way the pattern goes.
beats.coach: Squaring removes the sign: a falling fit can have this same r².

beats.spoken: For a prediction, substitute x into the fitted line. Do not use r or r squared as the slope.
beats.coach: Substitute into the fitted line: at x = 3.5, ŷ = 1.4(3.5) + 0.5 = 5.4. Both numbers are exact for these data.
